venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Baugh made FAU chase the crease. Philo took the short throw they kept giving him. White’s corners left seven yards of grass — 90 plays.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — broadcast sit plus GNFP public film cuts. Fan rail empty until Charles approves.
headline: Florida controlled Saturday because Jadan Baugh made FAU chase the run, and Aaron Philo took the throw FAU kept giving him. Faulkner’s idea was one run that creates a crease. White’s idea was two safeties deep. The leak was seven yards of grass — 90 plays.

offense.body:
Faulkner’s stressor: make FAU wrong about the crease, without changing how the play starts.

Philo lined up in the shotgun — five yards behind the center — and handed it to Baugh. The five linemen stepped in one direction. Two of them drove the same tackle. One climbed up to the linebacker. Baugh found the crease, got on the safety, and a play was made. The first run after DJ Coleman’s interception was that play: eight or nine yards up the middle from the 6. Florida came back to it on first down.

FAU had three ways to sit on that picture. Faulkner had three answers. If they played the crease straight, Baugh hit it or cut it back. He finished 14 carries, 160 yards, three rushing scores. The cutback is what he does. If they sat downhill and waited for that same hole, Faulkner changed who led him. Third-and-2 in the third quarter, Florida’s 33. The tight end on the left held FAU’s end inside. The left tackle ran around that block and led Baugh to the edge. Baugh followed him 61 yards to the 6 and scored from there on the next run. If they dropped the corner and left the safety deep — staying back, giving the short throw — Philo took it. That is Faulkner. Throw it short as often as they will let you. When they sat even softer, he threw it over the top. After FAU made it 17–7, TJ Abrams went 63 yards to the 8. Bailey Stockton’s first-quarter score was the other leftover: throw it now, let the line get out in front, walk it in from the 12.

The picture that kept FAU guessing was the motion before the snap. A receiver walked across. Philo and the staff were asking one question: are you running down to the line with him, or are you staying back? If a defender ran with the motion, Florida knew it was man. If he stayed, Florida knew it was zone. Same run start. Different answer.

Baugh got the space because the idea is built for him. He moved the chains on first down. Philo moved them when the corner dropped — Dallas Wilson for 19 on the opening drive, then the short stop-route and the throw to the sideline. The explosives came from the same idea. Vernell Brown III’s 49-yard touchdown started as a short throw to the right. The first man missed. Brown was already running. Abrams was the over-the-top when the safety was too far back. Baugh’s 61 was the edge when they sat on the crease.

Philo ran the operation. Opening drive, he worked his first read, saw the coverage, and went to Wilson. When he got the ball out on time, the idea was easy. When he held it, the play died. The interception was Micah Mays Jr. The ball came off his hands. Jayden Sweeney was sitting there.

The line was clean. One false start. No late-shift disaster. They climbed to the second level on the run that won the night. The mistake that loses a real game was not a missed block. Jake Moore snapped it over Philo’s head inside the 5. Florida lost twenty yards on that snap.
bullets: Play the crease straight and Baugh hits it or cuts it back — 14 for 160, three scores.
Sit downhill on third-and-2 and Faulkner changes who leads: tight end holds the end, left tackle leads Baugh 61 yards.
Stay back and Philo takes the short throw. Stay farther back and he throws it over the top — Abrams 63, Stockton from the 12.

defense.body:
White’s lever was the top of the defense. Four down. Extra defensive back. Two safeties deep. Standard four-man rush — Jayden Woods on the edge. Take away the throw over the top. The safety is there if they go deep. Live with the short throw if you tackle it.

The disguise was the linebackers walking up so it looked like more were coming, then dropping. Veltkamp would throw the middle and a linebacker was already there.

The throw that stayed open was the short one. FAU never huddled. They threw it short as often as they could, the entire game. Caden Veltkamp lived on Dom Henry and Kelby Valsin at five to eight yards. Florida’s corners started seven yards off and bailed. That is 90 plays. Jon Sumrall said it: on third-and-1, your corner cannot be nine yards off. That happened.

The job that failed was the cushion, the tackle after the catch, and the edge when Veltkamp kept it. Set the edge is the job. When the defender on the outside left, Veltkamp scored from the 7. Florida stuffed the run at the 1 and still lost the yard. Ethan Ervin from a yard out.

The jobs that succeeded were the ones where the defensive backs trusted the help over the top. Aaron Chiles and DJ Coleman jumped the throw-it-now screens — seal the outside, linebackers and tackles flow, kill it before it starts. Opening drive, third-and-10, Coleman sold the middle, peeled to the sideline, and intercepted it at Florida’s 5. Later he got a hand on another ball. Dijon Johnson caught that one. The four-man rush got a pocket push. The ball was out too fast for it to finish.

The structure killed the shot over the top. It allowed volume. Ninety plays. A 20-yard touchdown to Valsin.

The fix is force them to throw it over you. Do not back up and give the short throw. Tackle it. Set the edge when the quarterback runs.
bullets: Corners seven yards off and backing up. FAU threw it short all night. Ninety plays.
Four-man rush, Woods on the edge. The ball was out too fast to finish the sack.
Coleman sold the middle, then intercepted it at Florida’s 5. The fix is force the throw over you and set the edge.

specials.body: Patrick Durkin made a 53-yard field goal. Three points from a drive that stalled. Florida never punted. FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Stockton’s touchdown. Specials flipped the field once and added three. They did not give points away.
bullets: FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Stockton’s touchdown.

keys: Offense: hand it to Baugh, climb to the linebacker, take the short throw when they stay back, throw it over the top when they stay farther back.
Defense: two safeties deep, rush four, live with the short throw.
Leak: seven yards of grass. Ninety plays.
Fix: force the throw over you. Tackle the short throw. Set the edge.
Campbell throws it short and Sixkiller runs. That is the leak. Woods stays outside on the keep.

nextWeek.look: Campbell will throw it short and Sixkiller will run. That is the leak. Florida will still hand it to Baugh. Woods has to stay outside when Sixkiller keeps it.
